title: Segmentation fault when loading a Coral Edge TPU model
body: I am using TensorFlow 2.14.0 from a binary installation on Raspberry Pi OS Bookworm with Python 3.11.2. A YOLOv8 model converted to integer-quantized TFLite and compiled for the Coral Edge TPU crashes as soon as it is loaded. This happens on both a Raspberry Pi 5 with 8 GB RAM and a Raspberry Pi 4B with 2 GB RAM, and I reproduced it with TensorFlow Nightly. Under gdb, Python receives SIGSEGV in tflite::Subgraph::ReplaceNodeSubsetsWithDelegateKernels while libedgetpu.so.1 is applying the delegate. I included standalone Ultralytics code and the gdb stack trace.

symptoms_visible: My program crashes as soon as it loads the Edge TPU model.
Under gdb, Python receives SIGSEGV in tflite::Subgraph::ReplaceNodeSubsetsWithDelegateKernels while libedgetpu.so.1 is involved.
I see the same crash on a Raspberry Pi 5 and a Raspberry Pi 4B.
N0.label: N0 Edge TPU model load segfault reported

symptoms_visible: Loading my compiled Edge TPU model still produces the same segmentation fault.
N1.label: N1 model and runtime details collected

symptoms_visible: The notebook reports an error when it loads the model without the Coral delegate, while my program still segfaults when it loads the model for Edge TPU inference.
N1_x.label: N1_x custom-ops direction rejected

symptoms_visible: The same program crashes on my Raspberry Pi 4B with Python 3.9.2 and on my Raspberry Pi 5 in a Python 3.9.18 environment.
N2.label: N2 supported Python versions tested

symptoms_visible: The Edge TPU model still crashes across the TensorFlow AArch64 versions I tested.
I can reproduce the crash using only the Ultralytics export command, the Coral runtime installation, and the Ultralytics validation command.
N3.label: N3 crash isolated across TensorFlow versions

question_patterns: How was the TFLite model converted and compiled for the accelerator?
Can you confirm that this is an integer-quantized model compiled with the current Edge TPU compiler?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I converted the model to TFLite with int8 and compiled it using the latest Edge TPU compiler.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I passed an unquantized ordinary TFLite model directly to the Edge TPU without compiling it.
I used the previous compiler release, but recompiling with the latest one produces the same crash.

question_patterns: Which accelerator runtime is installed, and is the device firmware current?
Have you updated the Coral runtime and hardware software?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Edge TPU runtime is on the latest version available to me.

question_patterns: Which TFLite interpreter is Ultralytics invoking in this environment?
Are you loading this through TensorFlow's interpreter or a separate tflite-runtime package?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The Ultralytics module uses the TFLite interpreter from the TensorFlow module, if I remember correctly.

question_patterns: Can you share the compiled model file so it can be inspected?

edges.comment: Thread c0-c3, reporter's Raspberry Pi systems: maintainers asked about model/runtime correctness and requested the compiled model; the reporter described the int8 compilation, installed runtime, interpreter path, and shared the file.

solution.intent: Treat the notebook's unresolved operations as unsupported custom ops and direct the reporter to implement or register those custom ops.
solution.concrete_example: The supplied file appears to use custom ops in the notebook, so follow the TensorFlow Lite custom-operator instructions and ensure those operations are registered.

edges.comment: Thread c4-c5, reporter's model: a maintainer interpreted the delegate-less notebook result as custom ops. The reporter rejected that direction because the compiled model relies on the Coral USB accelerator delegate; no custom-op modification was made.

question_patterns: Can you test this with a supported Python 3.9 environment and report what happens?
Does the crash still occur under Python 3.9 rather than Python 3.11?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I previously tried the same program on a Raspberry Pi 4B with Python 3.9.2 and it had the same crash, although that Pi froze when I tried gdb. I also tried a Python 3.9.18 Anaconda environment on the Pi 5 and got the same crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It works under Python 3.9 and only crashes under Python 3.11.
Python 3.9.18 crashes in the same place, but I did not repeat the test on the Pi 4B.

question_patterns: Which Coral installation steps did you follow before the crash began?
Can you list how you installed the accelerator runtime?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I followed the installation instructions exactly as written on the Coral installation page.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I installed an unofficial runtime package from an unrelated repository and did not follow the Coral setup instructions.

edges.comment: Thread c7-c10, reporter's Raspberry Pi 4B and Pi 5: the maintainer asked for a supported Python-version test and installation details. The reporter supplied raw outcomes showing the same crash under two Python 3.9 environments and stated that the Coral instructions were followed.

question_patterns: Does changing the TensorFlow AArch64 version alter the crash?
Which other TensorFlow versions have you tested on the Pi?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried tensorflow-aarch64 2.13.1 and 2.15.0 and the crash still occurred. I also tested every TensorFlow version from the then-current latest down through 2.12.1 on a Raspberry Pi 4B with Python 3.9.2, with the same crash.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: TensorFlow 2.12.1 works, while every later version crashes.
I tested only 2.13.1, 2.14.0, and 2.15.0, and all three crash.

edges.comment: Thread c12-c14, reporter's Raspberry Pi systems: the reporter volunteered cross-version test results and a shorter Ultralytics CLI reproduction. The target node records the reproduction commands as volunteered information rather than attributing them to another participant.

question_patterns: Can you test the newly provided build with the same model and report whether it still crashes?
Please retest your case using the updated build and tell me what you observe.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I already tested participant4's builds a while ago, and they work without any issues on my Raspberry Pi 5 with Python 3.11.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The newly provided build still segfaults at model load on my Raspberry Pi 5.
The build works on my Raspberry Pi 5 with Python 3.11, but I have not retested the Pi 4B.

edges.comment: Thread c27-c28, reporter's Raspberry Pi 5: after the upstream library update, the maintainer requested a retest. The reporter's raw answer referred to earlier testing of participant4's builds and reported that the model ran without issues; it did not claim a separate retest of official master.

solution.intent: Use an updated Edge TPU runtime build that is compatible with the newer TensorFlow Lite runtime, rather than changing the model, downgrading Python, or modifying TensorFlow custom ops.
solution.concrete_example: Replace the older Edge TPU runtime with the updated library build that supports current TensorFlow Lite runtimes, then run the same compiled YOLOv8 Edge TPU model and verify that model loading no longer segfaults.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the delegate-related stack trace, failures across Python and TensorFlow versions, and the successful updated-build test. Mapping those observations to the accepted diagnosis—that the older libedgetpu runtime lacked compatibility with newer TensorFlow Lite runtimes—is the engineer-side inference established by the thread's final resolution.

edges.comment: Thread c15-c29: the reporter first reported success with participant4's updated runtime, participant4 later clarified that the upstream library still needed updating, and the library update was eventually merged. The reporter confirmed that the same updated builds already ran without issues on the original Pi 5/Python 3.11 setup. PR coordination and binary-release logistics are intentionally not scored.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause as an incompatibility between the older libedgetpu runtime and newer TensorFlow Lite runtime versions, not a TensorFlow model-loading bug alone.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the delegate-related stack trace, reproduction across Python 3.9 and 3.11 and multiple TensorFlow versions, and the successful test with an updated runtime build.
Must recommend using an updated compatible Edge TPU runtime build; rewriting custom ops or merely downgrading Python must not be presented as the fix.
Must not settle on the custom-ops direction, because the delegate-less notebook error was expected for this Edge TPU-compiled model and did not explain the delegate-time segmentation fault.
Must have the reporter verify the same model on an updated build before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Raspberry Pi and ML user who can convert and compile YOLO models, manage Python environments and TensorFlow versions, run gdb, and test alternative runtime builds.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and concise; supplies concrete reproduction commands and test outcomes, corrects suggestions that do not fit the Edge TPU delegate setup, and follows up after independently testing new builds.
